- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., -0.40 to -0.70); model tends to overshoot upward after sharp moves.
- Underestimate downward corrections when sentiment is mildly positive (e.g., 0.27–0.37) — model fails to anticipate mean reversion in early cycles.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility and underestimates downside risk.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true trend shifts — model often misses 1–2 day lagged reversals.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak (e.g., -0.70 → 0.29), model tends to overcorrect and overestimate price rise — apply downward bias adjustment.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in early 30d forecast, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — reduce initial forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 30d horizon.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment > -0.30 and price spikes > 2% from prior day, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
